results.proposal_summary: The Nature for Health (N4H) Phase II Expression of Interest, funded by Germany's BMUV through the International Climate Initiative (IKI) via a Multi-Partner Trust Fund, invites governments and regional intergovernmental entities from OECD DAC ODA-eligible countries to apply for up to USD 2,250,000 in seed funding to implement integrated, preventative One Health approaches addressing biodiversity loss, zoonotic spillover risk, and environmental determinants of health. The call is exclusively open to national governments, sub-national governmental entities, and regional intergovernmental bodies; non-governmental entities, including UN agencies, are explicitly ineligible. The application window ran from 10 January 2025 to 7 April 2025 (now closed), with selection of up to six Phase II partners planned for August 2025. Implementation periods are expected to last 2–3 years. No co-financing is universally required, though regional proposals involving non-ODA-eligible countries must secure co-funding for those components.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The call focuses on biodiversity, pandemic prevention, and One Health environmental integration, which lies outside the ILO's core mandate of labour standards, employment, social protection, and decent work.

results.proposal_summary: The Malaysia-UN SDG Trust Fund Call for Proposals 2024/2025, a partnership between the UN in Malaysia and Yayasan MySDG (supported by Malaysia's Ministry of Finance), invited innovative projects in Malaysia targeting marginalized and disadvantaged groups across three pillars: People & Prosperity, Planet, and Peace & Partnership. Grants ranged from USD 100,000 to USD 500,000 per proposal with a project duration of 6 to 18 months. Eligible applicants included Malaysia-based CSOs, NGOs, academic institutions, and UN agencies (PUNOs) that are members of the Malaysia UN Country Team and have signed the Fund's MOU; PUNOs were required to submit joint proposals with at least two UN organizations. The submission deadline was 4 November 2024, and the call is now closed.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The fund's priority areas include social protection for informal workers, skills training and decent jobs for the poor, addressing labour migration and rights of migrants/refugees, and promoting socioeconomic rights for marginalised groups — all directly aligned with the ILO's core decent work mandate.

results.proposal_summary: The UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) launched a £19.95 million, 5-year programme (2026–2031) titled HOPE-S to prevent and respond to violence against women and girls (VAWG) and conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV) in conflict-affected areas of Sudan. Eligible applicants included international NGOs, Sudanese national and local CSOs, United Nations agencies, not-for-profit academic institutions, and mixed consortia (with for-profit entities only permitted as downstream partners). results.proposal_summary: Norad (Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation) is issuing an invitation-based call for proposals targeting international civil society organisations (WPS-INGOs) with Women, Peace and Security as their core mandate, aligned with Norway's National Action Plan for WPS (2023–2030). The call supports interventions enabling women and girls to participate meaningfully in peace processes and political dialogue, with thematic priorities including women's participation in peace processes, implementation of peace/ceasefire agreements, transitional justice, CRSV/SGBV, and protection of women human rights defenders. Norad aims to enter into three to five agreements for the period 2027–2030 based on this call. Only pre-selected international WPS-INGOs, identified through a prior mapping exercise, have been invited to apply. No grant size is specified. The deadline for submission via the Grants Portal is 12 August 2026 at 13:00 CEST. The ILO is not eligible as the call explicitly targets international NGOs/civil society organisations.

results.proposal_summary: SECO (Switzerland) has launched its third call for proposals for Swiss private-sector investment in Ukraine's reconstruction, open from 27 May 2026 with a deadline of 20 September 2026. The call provides CHF 3–10 million per project from a total envelope of up to CHF 50 million, under Switzerland's CHF 500 million private-sector window within the Ukraine country programme 2025–2028. Eligible applicants are Swiss companies with an established presence in Ukraine that must contribute at least 50% of project costs. Funded activities focus on building production facilities for long-term manufacturing in Ukraine. Projects are selected in a two-stage process by a committee of Swiss and Ukrainian authorities. The ILO is not an eligible applicant as the call targets Swiss private companies only and is structured as a private-sector investment co-financing vehicle.

results.proposal_summary: Switzerland's State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) has launched the third call for proposals to co-finance investment projects by Swiss companies in Ukraine, supporting the country's reconstruction and economic recovery. The call is open exclusively to Swiss companies with an established presence in Ukraine and focuses on investment in the construction and reconstruction of production and operational facilities intended for long-term use. The federal government provides between CHF 3 million and CHF 10 million per project, with companies required to contribute at least 50% of total project costs. The call is part of Switzerland's CHF 1.5 billion country programme for Ukraine 2025–2028, with CHF 500 million allocated for Swiss private sector projects. The selection process runs until spring 2027, with applications due by 20 September 2026 via SECO's dedicated portal.

The federal government is contributing up to CHF 150 million in total, with individual project grants ranging from CHF 3 million to CHF 30 million. The call focuses on strengthening public infrastructure in Ukraine (energy, housing, public transport, health, demining). Only Swiss companies operating in Ukraine are eligible to apply. results.proposal_summary: The Common Fund for Commodities (CFC) has launched its 29th Call for Proposals, inviting applications from SMEs, cooperatives, social enterprises, NGOs, and public or private sector entities based in or operating within any of its 101 member countries. The call focuses on transformative projects that empower smallholder farmers, strengthen commodity value chains, and promote inclusive local development across thematic areas including regenerative agriculture, local value addition, agtech, financial access, and women entrepreneurship. Funding is provided exclusively through loans and other debt instruments, with a maximum of USD 1.5 million per regular project and up to USD 300,000 under the Fast-Track procedure; no non-reimbursable grant component is available. Applications must be submitted by 1 October 2026. Priority is given to proposals from or focused on LDCs, LLDCs, and SIDCs, as well as projects in the Congo Basin region. The ILO is not eligible as applicants must be SMEs, cooperatives, NGOs, or similar entities, and the funding instrument is a repayable loan.
results.ilo_match_evidence: While the call touches on smallholder livelihoods, women's economic empowerment, and decent work (SDG 8 indicators are referenced), its primary purpose is commercial loan financing to agribusinesses rather than technical assistance, labour standards, or social protection work within the ILO mandate.
